title: How Swift the Torrent Rolls
description: How Swift the Torrent Rolls in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 528 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"The Fathers, where are they?"”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How swift the tor-rent rolls, That bears us to the sea! The tide that bears our thought-less souls To vast e-ter-ni-ty!

lines: That bears us to the sea!
The tide that bears our thoughtless souls
With all they called their own?
Their joys, and griefs, and hopes and cares,
While we, as on life's utmost verge,
Till with them, in the land of light,

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
